properties.description: Foundry (formerly Azure AI Foundry) and Azure OpenAI - Spike in HTTP 401/403 or 429 responses on Foundry inference endpoints Analytic Rule template version 1.0.0

Sudden authentication failures indicate key stuffing or stolen-key probing; sustained HTTP 429 (QuotaExceeded) spikes from an unusual IP can signal API key leakage and unauthorised model consumption (denial-of-wallet). MITRE ATT&CK: Impact T1499 (Endpoint Denial of Service) and Credential Access T1110. Source guide: ai/azure-openai-ai-foundry/README.md (C2).
properties.displayName: Foundry (formerly Azure AI Foundry) and Azure OpenAI - Spike in HTTP 401/403 or 429 responses on Foundry inference endpoints
properties.query:
// CUSTOM - Burst of auth failures or throttling on Cognitive Services / Azure OpenAI endpoints
// ASSUMPTION: ResultSignature holds the HTTP status code string (for example "401", "403", "429")
// in AzureDiagnostics for RequestResponse / Audit categories. Confirm column name (ResultSignature
// vs StatusCode_d) on a sample row in your workspace before enabling.
AzureDiagnostics
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where ResourceProvider == "MICROSOFT.COGNITIVESERVICES"
| where Category in ("RequestResponse", "Audit")
| extend HttpStatus = coalesce(tostring(ResultSignature), tostring(column_ifexists("StatusCode_d", "")))
| where HttpStatus in ("401", "403", "429")
| summarize FailureCount = count(),
            Operations = make_set(OperationName, 10),
            Statuses = make_set(HttpStatus, 5)
            by Resource, CallerIPAddress, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where FailureCount >= 50
| project TimeGenerated, Resource, CallerIPAddress, FailureCount, Statuses, Operations

properties.description: 365 Copilot - Jailbreak or prompt injection flag detected in Copilot interactions Analytic Rule template version 1.0.0

Microsoft 365 Copilot records safety flags including JailbreakDetected inside message metadata. Alerting on repeated or targeted jailbreak detections catches adversarial prompting early. If you hunt in Defender XDR instead of Sentinel, run the equivalent check against CloudAppEvents where ActionType == "CopilotInteraction" and expand RawEventData.CopilotEventData.Messages. MITRE ATLAS: AML.T0051 (LLM Prompt Injection). Source guide: ai/microsoft-365-copilot/README.md (C1).
properties.displayName: 365 Copilot - Jailbreak or prompt injection flag detected in Copilot interactions
properties.query:
// CUSTOM - Jailbreak flag set in CopilotActivity interaction events
// ASSUMPTION: LLMEventData contains a Messages array with a boolean JailbreakDetected field,
// matching the Purview CopilotInteraction schema. Inspect a sample row in your tenant first.
CopilotActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where RecordType == "CopilotInteraction"
| extend Messages = LLMEventData.Messages
| mv-expand Message = Messages
| where tobool(Message.JailbreakDetected) == true
| summarize JailbreakCount = count(),
            AppHosts = make_set(AppHost, 10),
            Agents = make_set(AgentName, 10),
            SrcIPs = make_set(SrcIpAddr, 10)
            by ActorName, ActorUserId, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| project TimeGenerated, ActorName, ActorUserId, JailbreakCount, AppHosts, Agents, SrcIPs

properties.description: 365 Copilot - Unusual burst of Copilot prompts referencing sensitive files Analytic Rule template version 1.0.0

A compromised account or departing insider can use Copilot to summarise dozens of confidential files rapidly without triggering bulk SharePoint download thresholds. Tune resource_threshold against a 14-day baseline in your tenant, or filter specifically on your Confidential and Highly Confidential SensitivityLabelId GUIDs. MITRE ATT&CK: Collection T1213 (Data from Information Repositories). Source guide: ai/microsoft-365-copilot/README.md (C2).
properties.displayName: 365 Copilot - Unusual burst of Copilot prompts referencing sensitive files
properties.query:
// CUSTOM - Single user accessing many distinct resources via Copilot in one hour
// ASSUMPTION: LLMEventData.AccessedResources holds the array of grounded files with Id/Name
// and SensitivityLabelId properties, matching the Purview CopilotInteraction schema.
// Confirm exact key names on one sample row in your workspace before enabling.
let resource_threshold = 20;
CopilotActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where RecordType == "CopilotInteraction"
| extend Resources = LLMEventData.AccessedResources
| mv-expand Resource = Resources
| extend ResourceId = tostring(Resource.Id),
         SensitivityLabelId = tostring(Resource.SensitivityLabelId)
| where isnotempty(ResourceId)
| summarize DistinctResources = dcount(ResourceId),
            LabelledResources = dcountif(ResourceId, isnotempty(SensitivityLabelId)),
            SampleResources = make_set(ResourceId, 10),
            AppHosts = make_set(AppHost, 5),
            SrcIPs = make_set(SrcIpAddr, 5)
            by ActorName, ActorUserId, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where DistinctResources >= resource_threshold
| project TimeGenerated, ActorName, ActorUserId, DistinctResources, LabelledResources, AppHosts, SrcIPs, SampleResources

properties.description: Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) - Interactive exec or attach into a Kubernetes pod Analytic Rule template version 1.0.0

Attackers who obtain cluster credentials frequently run kubectl exec into running pods to steal mounted tokens, pivot or drop tools. MITRE: Execution, Container Administration Command T1609. Source guide: azure/aks/README.md (C1).
properties.displayName: Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) - Interactive exec or attach into a Kubernetes pod
properties.query:
// CUSTOM - Interactive exec or attach into a pod in AKS
// ASSUMPTION: Resource-specific diagnostic setting kube-audit-admin is enabled (writes to AKSAuditAdmin).
// Filter approved break-glass or SRE accounts via a watchlist after baselining.
let approved_users = dynamic(["sre-breakglass@yourdomain.gov.au"]);
AKSAuditAdmin
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where Verb in ("create", "get")
| where tostring(ObjectRef.resource) == "pods"
    and tostring(ObjectRef.subresource) in ("exec", "attach")
| extend Username = tostring(User.username),
         Namespace = tostring(ObjectRef.namespace),
         PodName = tostring(ObjectRef.name),
         ResponseCode = toint(ResponseStatus.code)
| where ResponseCode between (100 .. 299)
| where Username !startswith "system:"
| where Username !in~ (approved_users)
| project TimeGenerated, Cluster = _ResourceId, Username, Namespace, PodName,
          Subresource = tostring(ObjectRef.subresource), RequestUri, SourceIps, ResponseCode

properties.description: Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) - ClusterRoleBinding created or modified for privileged access Analytic Rule template version 1.0.0

Creating or modifying a ClusterRoleBinding (especially binding cluster-admin) grants cluster-wide control and is a classic Kubernetes persistence technique. MITRE: Privilege Escalation and Persistence, Account Manipulation T1098. Source guide: azure/aks/README.md (C2).
properties.displayName: Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) - ClusterRoleBinding created or modified for privileged access
properties.query:
// CUSTOM - ClusterRoleBinding created, updated or patched outside system controllers
// ASSUMPTION: Verify your GitOps controller service account name (e.g. Flux or ArgoCD) and add to allow list.
let gitops_accounts = dynamic(["system:serviceaccount:flux-system:kustomize-controller"]);
AKSAuditAdmin
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where Verb in ("create", "update", "patch")
| where tostring(ObjectRef.resource) in ("clusterrolebindings", "rolebindings")
| extend Username = tostring(User.username),
         BindingName = tostring(ObjectRef.name),
         Namespace = tostring(ObjectRef.namespace),
         ResponseCode = toint(ResponseStatus.code)
| where ResponseCode between (200 .. 299)
| where Username !startswith "system:apiserver"
    and Username !startswith "system:kube-controller-manager"
    and Username !in~ (gitops_accounts)
| project TimeGenerated, Cluster = _ResourceId, Verb, Username,
          ResourceType = tostring(ObjectRef.resource), Namespace, BindingName, SourceIps, RequestUri

properties.description: Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) - Static AKS cluster-admin credentials retrieved via Azure API Analytic Rule template version 1.0.0

Calling listClusterAdminCredential returns a static certificate-based cluster-admin kubeconfig that bypasses Entra ID Conditional Access and RBAC unless local accounts are disabled. If local accounts are disabled (--disable-local-accounts), this API call fails and any successful occurrence is an immediate severity-high incident. MITRE: Credential Access, Steal Application Access Token / Valid Accounts T1078.004. Source guide: azure/aks/README.md (C3).
properties.displayName: Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) - Static AKS cluster-admin credentials retrieved via Azure API
properties.query:
// CUSTOM - Retrieval of AKS static cluster-admin credentials via Azure Resource Manager
// ASSUMPTION: AzureActivity is connected for subscriptions hosting AKS clusters.
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where ActivityStatusValue in ("Success", "Succeeded")
| where OperationNameValue =~ "Microsoft.ContainerService/managedClusters/listClusterAdminCredential/action"
| project TimeGenerated, Caller, CallerIpAddress, SubscriptionId, ResourceGroup, Cluster = _ResourceId

properties.description: Azure SQL Database and Managed Instance - SQL authentication brute force followed by success Analytic Rule template version 1.0.0

Catches a client IP spraying or brute-forcing database logins and then succeeding within the same hour, which complements Defender for SQL alerts when auditing is active. MITRE: Credential Access, Brute Force T1110. Source guide: azure/azure-sql/README.md (C2).
properties.displayName: Azure SQL Database and Managed Instance - SQL authentication brute force followed by success
properties.query:
// CUSTOM - Multiple failed SQL authentications followed by a success from the same client IP
// ASSUMPTION: FAILED_DATABASE_AUTHENTICATION_GROUP and SUCCESSFUL_DATABASE_AUTHENTICATION_GROUP are enabled (on by default).
let lookback = 1h;
let failedThreshold = 15;
let failures = AzureDiagnostics
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where Category == "SQLSecurityAuditEvents"
    | where action_name_s == "DATABASE AUTHENTICATION FAILED"
    | summarize FailedCount = count(), FirstFail = min(TimeGenerated), LastFail = max(TimeGenerated),
                TargetedUsers = make_set(server_principal_name_s, 10)
        by client_ip_s, LogicalServerName_s, database_name_s
    | where FailedCount >= failedThreshold;
let successes = AzureDiagnostics
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where Category == "SQLSecurityAuditEvents"
    | where action_name_s == "DATABASE AUTHENTICATION SUCCEEDED"
    | summarize SuccessCount = count(), FirstSuccess = min(TimeGenerated),
                SucceededUsers = make_set(server_principal_name_s, 10)
        by client_ip_s, LogicalServerName_s, database_name_s;
failures
| join kind=inner successes on client_ip_s, LogicalServerName_s, database_name_s
| where FirstSuccess >= FirstFail
| project FirstFail, FirstSuccess, LogicalServerName_s, database_name_s, client_ip_s,
          FailedCount, SuccessCount, TargetedUsers, SucceededUsers

properties.description: Defender for Cloud - High-severity Defender for Cloud alert on a resource with active unhealthy recommendations Analytic Rule template version 1.0.0

Correlating active workload alerts with open high-severity recommendations surfaces compromised resources that also have known exposure paths. MITRE: Initial Access and Privilege Escalation (tactics inherit from the underlying alert). Source guide: azure/defender-for-cloud/README.md (C2).
properties.displayName: Defender for Cloud - High-severity Defender for Cloud alert on a resource with active unhealthy recommendations
properties.query:
// CUSTOM - High-severity Defender for Cloud alert on an asset with High unhealthy recommendations
// ASSUMPTION: Continuous export for Security recommendations is active and AssessedResourceId
// matches CompromisedEntity or ResourceId formats in your tenant. Inspect one sample join first.
let unhealthy = SecurityRecommendation
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(2d)
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, RecommendationState, RecommendationSeverity, RecommendationDisplayName)
        by AssessedResourceId, RecommendationId
    | where RecommendationState =~ "Unhealthy" and RecommendationSeverity =~ "High"
    | summarize OpenHighRecs = count(), SampleRecs = make_set(RecommendationDisplayName, 5)
        by ResourceKey = tolower(AssessedResourceId);
SecurityAlert
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where AlertSeverity =~ "High"
| where ProductName has_any ("Defender for Cloud", "Azure Security Center")
| extend ResourceKey = tolower(ResourceId)
| join kind=inner unhealthy on ResourceKey
| project TimeGenerated, AlertName, AlertSeverity, CompromisedEntity, ResourceId, OpenHighRecs, SampleRecs

properties.description: Azure Key Vault - Key Vault secret list and read sweep by a human user Analytic Rule template version 1.0.0

Applications fetch specific known secrets by name. Human users listing all secrets (SecretList) and then reading multiple secrets (SecretGet) in quick succession is a classic manual credential-dumping pattern. MITRE: Credential Access, Unsecured Credentials T1552. Source guide: azure/key-vault/README.md (C1).
properties.displayName: Azure Key Vault - Key Vault secret list and read sweep by a human user
properties.query:
// CUSTOM - Human caller lists secrets then reads multiple secrets within 15 minutes
// ASSUMPTION: Identity JSON in AZKVAuditLogs contains claim.upn for interactive user tokens.
// Inspect one sample row of AZKVAuditLogs (project Identity, OperationName, RequestUri) before enabling.
AZKVAuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where OperationName in ("SecretList", "SecretGet")
| where ResultType =~ "Success" or HttpStatusCode == 200
| extend IdentityJson = parse_json(Identity)
| extend UserUpn = tostring(IdentityJson.claim.upn)
| where isnotempty(UserUpn)
| summarize Listed = countif(OperationName == "SecretList"),
            SecretsRead = dcountif(RequestUri, OperationName == "SecretGet"),
            SampleUris = make_set_if(RequestUri, OperationName == "SecretGet", 10),
            IPs = make_set(CallerIpAddress, 5)
            by UserUpn, _ResourceId, Window = bin(TimeGenerated, 15m)
| where Listed >= 1 and SecretsRead >= 5

properties.description: Azure Key Vault - Repeated unauthorised (403) Key Vault access attempts Analytic Rule template version 1.0.0

A spike in 403 Forbidden responses against a vault often means a compromised identity is probing vaults to see which secrets it can read, or an attacker's IP hit a Key Vault firewall rule. MITRE: Discovery and Credential Access, Cloud Infrastructure Discovery T1580. Source guide: azure/key-vault/README.md (C2).
properties.displayName: Azure Key Vault - Repeated unauthorised (403) Key Vault access attempts
properties.query:
// CUSTOM - Burst of Forbidden (403) Key Vault data plane requests
// ASSUMPTION: HttpStatusCode is numeric 403 and ResultSignature contains Forbidden in AZKVAuditLogs.
// Confirm both fields with a sample 403 row in your workspace.
AZKVAuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where HttpStatusCode == 403 or ResultSignature has "Forbidden"
| summarize DeniedCount = count(),
            Operations = make_set(OperationName, 10),
            Vaults = make_set(_ResourceId, 10)
            by CallerIpAddress, Identity = tostring(Identity)
| where DeniedCount >= 10
| order by DeniedCount desc

properties.description: Azure networking (VNet flow logs, Azure Firewall, WAF, DNS and DDoS) - Threat Intelligence or high-severity IDPS traffic allo... Analytic Rule template version 1.0.0

Catches cases where Azure Firewall Threat Intelligence or IDPS is set to Alert-only mode (or a policy exception let traffic pass) and an internal workload actually reached a known malicious destination. MITRE: Command and Control T1071, Initial Access T1190. Source guide: azure/network-nsg-flow-firewall/README.md (C1).
properties.displayName: Azure networking (VNet flow logs, Azure Firewall, WAF, DNS and DDoS) - Threat Intelligence or high-severity IDPS traffic allo...
properties.query:
// CUSTOM - Allowed traffic matching Azure Firewall Threat Intelligence or high-severity IDPS
// ASSUMPTION: Action value for alert-only/allowed traffic is "Alert" or "Allow" in your firewall policy.
// Inspect distinct Action values in AZFWThreatIntel and AZFWIdpsSignature before enabling.
let tiHits = AZFWThreatIntel
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
    | where Action !~ "Deny"
    | project TimeGenerated, Signal = "ThreatIntel", Action, SourceIp, DestinationIp,
              DestinationPort, Protocol, Target = coalesce(Fqdn, TargetUrl, DestinationIp),
              Detail = ThreatDescription, Firewall = _ResourceId;
let idpsHits = AZFWIdpsSignature
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
    | where Severity == 1 and Action !~ "Deny"
    | project TimeGenerated, Signal = "IDPS-High", Action, SourceIp, DestinationIp,
              DestinationPort, Protocol, Target = DestinationIp,
              Detail = strcat(Category, ": ", Description, " (Sig ", SignatureId, ")"),
              Firewall = _ResourceId;
union tiHits, idpsHits

properties.description: Azure Storage - Anonymous blob access on an account that shouldn't be public Analytic Rule template version 1.0.0

Even when public blob access is meant to be disabled by policy, exceptions happen. Catching AuthenticationType == "Anonymous" on sensitive accounts gives immediate visibility into accidental exposure. MITRE: Collection, Data from Cloud Storage T1530. Source guide: azure/storage/README.md (C1).
properties.displayName: Azure Storage - Anonymous blob access on an account that shouldn't be public
properties.query:
// CUSTOM - Successful anonymous read or list against sensitive blob storage accounts
// ASSUMPTION: AuthenticationType uses "Anonymous" and StatusCode is 200 in StorageBlobLogs.
// Populate public_allowlist with any intentionally public static-website or CDN storage accounts.
let public_allowlist = dynamic(["publicwebassets01"]);
StorageBlobLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where AuthenticationType =~ "Anonymous"
| where StatusCode == 200
| where AccountName !in~ (public_allowlist)
| summarize Requests = count(),
            BytesOut = sum(ResponseBodySize),
            Operations = make_set(OperationName, 10),
            IPs = make_set(CallerIpAddress, 10)
            by AccountName
| where Requests >= 5

properties.description: Azure Storage - Mass blob or file deletion burst Analytic Rule template version 1.0.0

Ransomware operators and destructive insiders often wipe blob containers or Azure File shares after exfiltration. Tune the threshold against legitimate batch cleanup jobs and Azure Storage lifecycle management policies. MITRE: Impact, Data Destruction T1485. Source guide: azure/storage/README.md (C2).
properties.displayName: Azure Storage - Mass blob or file deletion burst
properties.query:
// CUSTOM - High volume of blob deletions by a single caller IP within 15 minutes
// ASSUMPTION: OperationName values include DeleteBlob and DeleteContainer in StorageBlobLogs,
// and StatusCode 202 indicates accepted deletion. Verify with a test deletion first.
let lifecycle_allowlist = dynamic(["backup-cleanup-account"]);
StorageBlobLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where Category == "StorageDelete"
| where StatusCode in (200, 202)
| where AccountName !in~ (lifecycle_allowlist)
| summarize Deletes = count(),
            Operations = make_set(OperationName, 10),
            AuthTypes = make_set(AuthenticationType, 5),
            SampleUris = make_set(Uri, 10)
            by AccountName, CallerIpAddress, Window = bin(TimeGenerated, 15m)
| where Deletes >= 100
| order by Deletes desc

| where EventID == 7045

properties.description: Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS) - Directory change on the AD FS configuration container Analytic Rule template version 1.0.0

The AD FS configuration, including token-signing and token-decryption certificate references, lives in AD under the ADFS container. A 5136 change there is either the annual AutoCertificateRollover or an attacker adding their own signing material. Baseline the change rate for a month, then alert on anything outside it. Requires Audit Directory Service Changes and the AD FS container auditing SACL, both covered by MDI's automatic auditing or the manual steps (AD FS container auditing). MITRE: Credential Access T1552.004 and Persistence T1098. Expect roughly one change per certificate rollover per year, so a burst is a compromise signal, not tuning noise. Source guide: identity/adfs/README.md (C2).

| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where isnotempty(Location)
| summarize Countries = dcount(Location), SampleCountries = make_set(Location, 8),

properties.description: Entra ID (sign-in, audit and Graph activity logs) - Dormant service principal suddenly active Analytic Rule template version 1.0.0

A dormant app waking up is often a decommissioned integration left with valid credentials, sometimes a compromised one. MITRE: Initial Access and Persistence, valid accounts T1078.004. Source guide: identity/entra-id/README.md (C2).
properties.displayName: Entra ID (sign-in, audit and Graph activity logs) - Dormant service principal suddenly active
properties.query:
// CUSTOM - Service principal with no successful sign-ins for 60 days suddenly signs in
// ASSUMPTION: ResultType 0 means success, matching the documented SigninLogs convention.
// Confirm with a sample before enabling.
let baseline = AADServicePrincipalSignInLogs
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(60d) .. ago(1d))
    | where ResultType == "0"
    | summarize LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by ServicePrincipalId;
AADServicePrincipalSignInLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ResultType == "0"
| join kind=leftanti baseline on ServicePrincipalId
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), SignIns = count(),
            IPs = make_set(IPAddress, 10), Resources = make_set(ResourceDisplayName, 10)
            by ServicePrincipalId, ServicePrincipalName

properties.description: Linux (Syslog, CEF and auditd) - SSH brute force followed by a successful login Analytic Rule template version 1.0.0
MITRE: Credential Access T1110 (Brute Force) and Initial Access T1078 (Valid Accounts). Source guide: servers/linux-syslog/README.md (C1).
properties.displayName: Linux (Syslog, CEF and auditd) - SSH brute force followed by a successful login
properties.query:
// CUSTOM - Multiple failed SSH authentication attempts followed by an Accepted login from the same IP
// ASSUMPTION: OpenSSH logs to auth or authpriv with standard "Failed password" and "Accepted" strings.
// Verify exact SyslogMessage format on your Linux distros before enabling.
let failed = Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where Facility in ("auth", "authpriv") and ProcessName == "sshd"
| where SyslogMessage has "Failed password"
| extend SrcIP = extract(@"from ([0-9a-fA-F\.:]+) port", 1, SyslogMessage)
| where isnotempty(SrcIP)
| summarize FailCount = count(), FirstFail = min(TimeGenerated), LastFail = max(TimeGenerated)
            by Computer, SrcIP
| where FailCount >= 10;
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where Facility in ("auth", "authpriv") and ProcessName == "sshd"
| where SyslogMessage has "Accepted "
| extend SrcIP = extract(@"from ([0-9a-fA-F\.:]+) port", 1, SyslogMessage)
| join kind=inner failed on Computer, SrcIP
| where TimeGenerated >= FirstFail
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SrcIP, FailCount, SyslogMessage
